claim_boundary: Partial paper scope reviews; no automatic inference rules. Exact source edits invalidate reviews.

claims.title: Separate route outcomes from reusable identities
claims.statement: A failed route and a valid auxiliary identity have different truth statuses. Finite certificates and truncated ledger summaries do not certify full paper coverage.
requires: Separate identity scope from failed route

claims.title: W1 measure dictionary with convention lock
claims.statement: The source distinguishes measure identities, tent and B-spline reads, pole corrections, origin conventions and rebinning. A scalar identification without the stated corrections is not an exact full-domain positivity transfer.
requires: Correct Lerch sign and origin scheme
Bounds on the actual test domain

claims.title: W1 differentiated mean-zero versus odd test sector
claims.statement: Mean zero of derivatives of H1_0 tests is automatic; oddness of the undifferentiated tests is an additional sector restriction. These are not the same full-domain coverage statement.
requires: Explicit parity reduction or full test coverage

papers.title: W3: alias detector and smoothing limits

claims.title: W3 signed alias-comb identity
claims.statement: The finite window admits a zero-side alias-comb reading with pole terms. Nonnegativity on real frequencies does not establish that every relevant zero has real frequency.

claims.title: C=1 is direction-specific, not an operator bound
claims.statement: The C=1 discussion is confined to the pole-killed lock direction. The full-space operator reading is rejected; density averages alone do not establish the required supremum budget.
requires: No upgrade from average to supremum

claims.title: Fejer smoothing does not provide arbitrary resolution
claims.statement: Fejer smoothing connects the symbol to the zero density. Smoothing-width restrictions, off-line contributions and tail control must remain explicit; a smoothed bound is not pointwise positivity.
requires: Unconditional treatment of complex zero frequencies

claims.title: HP limit needs more than finite spectral matches
claims.statement: Finite states and measured spectral convergence do not supply a global Hilbert–Polya operator. Tightness, spectral identification, compatible limits and independent positivity retain their own proof obligations.
requires: Tightness proved on the growing family

claims.title: Four Lean modules are finite algebraic anchors
claims.statement: The paper names 116 public theorem declarations in four finite-algebra modules. Source discovery is not fresh kernel validation or an automatic proof of the paper's measurement and limit layers.
requires: Fresh type and axiom audit for selected declarations

claims.title: Paper PROVED labels are not kernel certificates
claims.anchor: Every load-bearing claim below is typed
claims.statement: The paper's PROVED convention includes finite floating-point residuals. Importing this label as a machine-checked mathematical theorem would conflate different evidence standards.
requires: Separate symbolic identity, rational certificate and floating residual

claims.title: Certified rung with all H1–H3 premises
claims.statement: The rung bounds delta by shat-transpose times inverse-U times shat. It assumes fine-level positive definiteness, exact nesting and a certified positive majorant, and uses the carried coarse solution.
requires: U positive definite and certified majorant

claims.title: Chain strictness needs nonvanishing review
claims.statement: The rung permits zero residual, while the chain proof invokes strictly positive rung contributions. A nonvanishing argument for the actual admissible family must be supplied before importing this strict conclusion.
requires: Actual-family nonvanishing or independent strict base
Do not mistake arbitrary matrices for admissible arithmetic windows

claims.title: Multilevel continuation beyond finite certificates
claims.statement: Window-by-window Cholesky results do not prove a cofinal family. The new Schur complements, admissible domains and residual increments require control at every needed level; a fixed positive margin is not presumed.

claims.title: Unproved alternative inverse-corner route
claims.statement: The paper names a separate corner route requiring sign and summed Harnack-type ratio control of inverse increments. Observations on sampled windows do not supply those assumptions uniformly.

claims.title: Normalized total-variation floor
claims.statement: The total-variation floor uses the exact admissibility normalization x_1=1 and the parity spectral gap. It is not a no-go for arbitrary normalization or unrestricted vectors.
requires: Specified parity basis and spectral gap

claims.title: Rank-three compression preserves joint arithmetic data
claims.statement: The comb–comb determinant depends on three linear functionals. Compression does not bound their joint position relative to the archimedean block and does not itself prove positivity.
requires: Joint arithmetic control of all three functionals

claims.title: Universal rank-two indefiniteness is false
claims.statement: For J with signature (1,2), P=((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1)) gives P-transpose J P / 2 = -I_2. Rank two alone does not imply indefiniteness; the rank and inertia upper bounds remain valid.
requires: Claim restricted to the printed universal arbitrary-P sentence

claims.title: R1 joint normalized determinant rate
claims.statement: The uniform rate for 1-r_12 squared is an open joint-cancellation problem. Neither the observed rate nor an asserted RH equivalence is supplied by this paper.
requires: Separate any intended implication to RH

papers.title: Gaussian E8 code: finite quotient certificates

claims.title: Gaussian finite certificates do not formalize every identification
claims.anchor: Honest scope of the formal layer
claims.statement: Lean covers explicit Smith maps, matrices and a fixed root list. The actual quotient-module construction, root-list completeness and parts of the invariant-theory identification remain separate from those finite certificates.

claims.title: Finite Gaussian code needs an independent arithmetic bridge
claims.statement: The Gaussian-code paper asserts finite algebra and explicitly no arithmetic or RH consequence. A finite code alone does not realize the full signed Weil form.
requires: Compatible growing carrier and independent positivity
